summary: A council turns down a supportive housing project, the state and the developer sue, and the city pays and moves the project to another site.
realLife: Elk Grove's council rejected the 67-unit Oak Rose Apartments in July 2022, saying the site did not meet its zoning standards. California sued in May 2023 under state housing law; the city settled with the developer in February 2024 to move the project to city land and with the state in September 2024, agreeing to pay $150,000 in fees, report on future housing and find another site to rezone.
sources: California Governor's Office, settlement over Elk Grove denial of housing project, Sep 4, 2024: https://www.gov.ca.gov/2024/09/04/governor-newsom-and-attorney-general-bonta-announce-settlement-resolving-elk-groves-unlawful-denial-of-housing-project/
